title: Bring Japan Home With You (Japanese Pantry Staples) | Kenji Eats Japan
contentHtml:
Follow along as we walk you through every aisle in a Japanese grocery store for a complete guide on stocking your pantry. This extended cut is exclusive for Patreon!

Community & Content Manager Erin here with our very last episode of the Kenji Eats Japan series!

Earlier this year, our team traveled to Japan in search of good food and even better kitchen knives (get the full story here). We knew we had to bring some of that culinary magic back for you. That’s why, today, we’re walking you through how to make that a reality with Kenji’s ultimate guide on How to Stock a Japanese Pantry.

Kenji Ate Japan… Now You Can, Too!

If you’re at all familiar with Japanese cuisine, you might be able to guess some of the basics Kenji will recommend: Soy sauce, miso paste, dashi, maybe a shiso leaf if you’re feeling fancy. But unlike most pantry hauls, this one is not just scratching the surface.

With the help of our local Japanese grocery store, we walked down each aisle and covered everything from ginkgo nuts and shungiku greens to different types of fish roe, cooking sauces, seaweeds, and more. We debated the tenets of microwavable rice (we’re not mad about it); whether you should make Japanese curry from scratch (probably not); and if you should stick to powdered wasabi or cash out on the real root (at $299.99 per pound? We’ll stick to the S&B tins, please)!

Special thank you to Uwajimaya for allowing us to film in their Seattle location for this video. If you’re ever in the area, we must recommend a visit to this iconic grocery shop—you won’t be disappointed with what you find.

How To Stock A Japanese Pantry (Extended)

All Frienjis here on Patreon can enjoy the extended cut of the video above. You can also dive into the full written article by Kenji here: How to Stock a Japanese Pantry 🔗

Now sit back and enjoy the haul! And don’t forget, Super Frienjis enjoy exclusive access to the written recipes from this series. If you haven't already, consider joining today to put your newly-stocked pantry to the test!

Thank you for supporting Kenji Eats Japan!

This series has been something special for our team to work on. We know it’s a little different from the content you’re used to and we are so grateful for your support.

Now, our team is getting started on the next big batch of content we’ll be bringing you. Keep your eyes peeled, Frienjis!

— Erin, Community & Content Manager
